content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing gradual mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 76+ levels) are common, followed by underestimation in subsequent days.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum after high peaks; often underestimates the depth of corrections.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent low prices; tend to be too optimistic when recent history is weak.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds onto high forecasts longer than observed price behavior.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility, especially in the first 5–7 days, then settles into a lower range too quickly.
